content.page_context: Clinical guideline recommendations on diagnosis of pulmonary embolism (PE), focusing on D-dimer thresholds, use of clinical probability (YEARS model), and imaging strategies.

D-dimer_and_YEARS_model.YEARS_rule: D-dimer cut-offs adapted to clinical probability according to the YEARS model (signs of DVT, haemoptysis, and whether an alternative diagnosis is less likely than PE).
cutoffs: PE excluded in patients without clinical items and D-dimer < 1000 µg/L
PE excluded in patients with one or more clinical items and D-dimer < 500 µg/L
D-dimer_and_YEARS_model.note: Low level of recommendation given limitations summarized elsewhere (Table 5 reference).

general_principles.clinical_evaluation: Diagnostic strategy should be based on clinical probability assessed by clinical judgement or a validated prediction rule.
general_principles.anticoagulation: In suspected high-risk PE (haemodynamic instability) initiate anticoagulation (e.g. UFH with weight-adjusted bolus) without delay; in patients with high or intermediate clinical probability initiation of anticoagulation is recommended without delay while diagnostic workup in progress.

D-dimer_measurement.recommendation: Plasma D-dimer measurement using a highly sensitive assay is recommended in outpatients/emergency department patients with low or intermediate clinical probability, or those that are PE-unlikely, to reduce unnecessary imaging.
D-dimer_measurement.age_adjusted: An age-adjusted D-dimer cut-off (age x 10 µg/L for patients aged >50 years) may be considered to exclude PE in patients with low or intermediate clinical probability.
D-dimer_measurement.limitations: D-dimer measurement is not recommended to exclude PE in patients with high clinical probability because a normal result does not safely rule out PE.

CTPA_recommendations.use: CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) recommended for suspected high-risk PE and to confirm/exclude PE depending on clinical probability.
interpretation_guidance: Reject diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if CTPA is normal in a patient with low or intermediate clinical probability.
Accept diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if CTPA shows a segmental or more proximal filling defect in a patient with intermediate or high clinical probability.
If CTPA is normal in a patient with high clinical probability, consider further testing; do not automatically exclude PE.
CTPA_recommendations.adjuncts: CT venography not recommended as an adjunct to CTPA.

VQ_scintigraphy: Reject diagnosis of PE (without further testing) if perfusion lung scan is normal.
Consider diagnosis of PE if V/Q scan yields high probability.
A non-diagnostic V/Q scan can be used to exclude PE when combined with a negative proximal compression ultrasound (CUS) in patients with low clinical probability or who are PE-unlikely.
VQ_scintigraphy_and_SPECT.VQ_SPECT: V/Q SPECT may be considered for PE diagnosis.

lower_limb_CUS.use: Accept diagnosis of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and (by extension) PE if CUS shows a proximal DVT in a patient with clinical suspicion of PE.
lower_limb_CUS.limitations: If CUS shows only a distal DVT, further testing should be considered to confirm PE. If a positive proximal CUS is used to confirm PE, assessment of PE severity should be considered for risk-adjusted management.

content.MRA: Magnetic resonance angiography (MRA) is not recommended for ruling out PE.
content.table_notes: Recommendations in the referenced table include class (I/IIa/IIb/III) and level (A/B/C) gradings for individual statements; specific gradings are provided in the original table image.
